people.name: Youngmoon Lee

people.current_position: Associate Professor, Department of Robotics (jointly Applied AI), Hanyang University ERICA; Director, RAISE Lab

bio.summary: Youngmoon Lee is an associate professor in the Robotics Department at Hanyang University ERICA and founding director of the RAISE Lab. Lee earned a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering from the Real-Time Computing Lab at the University of Michigan and a BS in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Seoul National University. Research focuses on real-time AI/ML, robot learning, and embedded and cyber-physical systems.
notable: Engineering Education Early Career Award, Korean Society for Engineering Education (2023)

people.name: Arun Ganesan
people.current_position: Meta (Facebook), New York City (per Shin's student list)

bio.summary: Arun Ganesan received a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Michigan in 2020 under Kang G. Shin. The dissertation studied using sensor redundancy between vehicles and smartphones for driving security and safety, including detecting CAN bus injection attacks with phone sensors.
bio.thesis_title: Using Sensor Redundancy in Vehicles and Smartphones for Driving Security and Safety

people.current_position: Assistant Professor, School of Computing and Information Systems, Singapore Management University

bio.summary: Dongyao Chen is an assistant professor at the School of Computing and Information Systems, Singapore Management University, where Chen leads the Flux Lab. Chen earned a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Michigan. Research covers multimodal sensing (e.g., magnetic fields), sensing security, and interactive systems.
bio.thesis_title: Seamless Interactions Between Humans and Mobility Systems

people.name: Timothy Trippel (jointly with Mattew Hicks at Virginia Tech)

bio.summary: Timothy Trippel received a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Michigan in 2021, co-advised by Kang G. Shin and Matthew Hicks. The dissertation addressed trustworthy hardware through security-driven design and verification, and Trippel co-authored 'Fuzzing Hardware Like Software' (USENIX Security 2022) with collaborators from Google.
bio.thesis_title: Developing Trustworthy Hardware with Security-Driven Design and Verification

people.name: Chun-Yu (Daniel) Chen

bio.summary: Chun-Yu (Daniel) Chen is a research scientist at Meta Platforms who completed a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Michigan in August 2022. Research spans mobile sensing, automotive systems, system security, privacy, and IoT. Chen received a MobiCom 2019 Best Poster Award.
bio.thesis_title: Context-Aware Detection and Resolution of Data Anomalies for Semi-Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems
notable: MobiCom 2019 Student Research Competition, second place

people.name: Duc Hoang Bui
people.current_position: Member of Technical Staff, Microsoft AI

bio.summary: Duc Bui received a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Michigan in 2022 under Kang G. Shin at the Real-Time Computing Lab. Research covers user privacy, program analysis, and natural language processing, particularly how mobile and web apps handle data versus their stated privacy policies. Bui now works on privacy compliance systems at Microsoft AI.
bio.thesis_title: Assessment of Privacy Risks in Mobile and Web Applications/Services

people.name: Mert Dieter Pese
people.current_position: Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Clemson University; Founding Director, TigerSec Laboratory

bio.summary: Mert D. Pesé is an assistant professor of computer science at Clemson University and founding director of the TigerSec Laboratory. Pesé earned a PhD in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Michigan in 2022 and MSc and dual BSc degrees from Technische Universität München. Research focuses on autonomous and connected vehicle security, trustworthy embodied AI, and automotive data privacy.
